Instrument.name: The Short-Wavelength Spectrograph Primary (SWP) Camera for IUE
Instrument.description: The IUE Short-Wavelength Spectrograph was an ultraviolet spectrograph covering the range of 1150 to 2000 angstroms. It could be operated in two dispersion modes: High resolution mode incorporated both an echelle grating as well as cross-dispersion; low resolution made use of only the cross-disperser. The spectrograph had two identical cameras, secondary emission cathode (SEC) Vidicons with ultraviolet converters. One was identified as "Prime" (SWP) and one as "Redundant" (SWR). In the case of the Short-Wavelength Spectrograph, only the Prime camera was fully operational for the mission.
